findings.affected_surface: §2.5 implementer constraint block and P2 Group-S Stop stdout
findings.claim: The implementer-copied §2.5 list still omits the Stop additionalContext inversion, so a P2 Group-S change can emit Group-T-style additionalContext on Stop and re-enter the multi-fire Stop loop the probe ruled unusable.
findings.evidence: Frozen R10 says using Stop additionalContext is forbidden in §2.5. Plan §2.5 lists Node/fail-open, byte-identical wording, no permissionDecision, inline queue writers, no sync-version, new suites, and no CHANGELOG/version/plugin.json edits, and never says Stop paths must not emit hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. P2 tells Group-S hooks to enqueue in addition to existing stderr and to keep any systemMessage, which does not forbid also writing Stop additionalContext. Plan §0 and the channel-probe V4 ruling record that Stop additionalContext is accepted and re-fires Stop about nine times per turn, derailing the answer.
findings.evidence_reference: Frozen rubric R10; plan §2.5, §4 P2, §0 Stop additionalContext bullet, §6 inversion; docs/plans/evidence/2026-09-26-hook-channel-probe/RULING.md V4
findings.repair: Add a §2.5 bullet copied into every implementer dispatch: Stop/Group-S paths never emit hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext or permissionDecision; they only append the documented queue line plus the existing stderr/systemMessage. P2 tests assert Stop advisory stdout contains neither additionalContext nor permissionDecision.

findings.affected_surface: P1 opt-in-multiplexer merge versus sibling exit-2 children
findings.claim: The folded multiplexer merge writes one JSON object with every child additionalContext, so an exit-2 block sibling that today has empty stdout would start carrying advisory JSON on the same blocked invocation.
findings.evidence: Plan §3 requires parsing each child stdout, merging additionalContext with newlines, preserving deny/ask (deny wins), and writing exactly one JSON object. It does not mention children that block with exit 2 and empty stdout. hooks/opt-in-multiplexer.js PreToolUse runs branch-protection before exec-boundary and commit-secret-scan; branch-protection still blocks direct commits with exit 2 and stderr only, while the merge/rebase warning at about line 92 is the Group-T advisory that will emit additionalContext. Today a warn-plus-exit-2 multiplexer invocation has empty stdout and a non-zero exit. After the stated merge it would emit additionalContext JSON on that same exit-2 invocation, which frozen R3 says must stay untouched.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan §3 multiplexer paragraph; hooks/opt-in-multiplexer.js EVENT_TABLE PreToolUse and stdout passthrough loop; hooks/branch-protection.js commit exit-2 path versus merge/rebase warning path; frozen rubric R3 and R8
findings.repair: Pin the P1 merge contract: forward only permissionDecision deny or ask (deny wins, never allow). When any child exits non-zero, keep that exit code and keep multiplexer stdout empty unless a child already emitted deny/ask JSON, in which case forward that decision object without attaching additionalContext. Put a warn-plus-exit-2 case in the new suite beside the two-advising-children case.

findings.affected_surface: P2 Group-S writer wording versus the no-shared-module rule
findings.claim: P2 still tells Group-S hooks to call enqueue, which contradicts the inline-only queue writers required by §2.5 and §3 and is the shape that recreates a shared queue helper.
findings.evidence: Plan §2.5 and §3 require each Group-S hook to inline its own O_APPEND against the documented jsonl format, with only advisory-relay.js reading the file, and they no longer name a shared queue module. P2 still opens with Group-S hooks call enqueue in addition to their existing stderr. That call-shaped leftover is enough for an implementer following the phase text to add a shared enqueue helper while §2.5 forbids a shared runtime module between hooks, including for the Stop queue.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan §2.5 no-shared-module and Group-S inline-append bullets; plan §3 queue FILE FORMAT; plan §4 P2 first sentence
findings.repair: Rewrite P2 so each Group-S hook inlines the documented one-line O_APPEND and fail-open wrap locally. Do not name enqueue as a callable and do not add a shared queue module.

findings.affected_surface: advisory-queue jsonl contract used by Group-S writers and advisory-relay.js
findings.claim: The documented queue format does not pin timestamp encoding, missing session_id behavior, or whole-line capping, so inlined writers can desynchronize, mix sessions, or corrupt the default-on queue into a fail-open no-delivery path.
findings.evidence: §3 defines each line as {ts, source, text}, says each writer O_APPENDs then trims to the newest 20 entries / 8 KiB, and keys strictly on payload session_id. ts as ISO string versus Unix milliseconds is unspecified, so inlined 24h checks can drop every line or none. Empty session_id is not told to skip; scripts/lib/live-state-dir.js maps empty to unknown, which would share one queue across sessions. Writer-side read-slice-rewrite trim races with the separate Stop registrations in hooks/hooks.json (opt-in multiplexer and default-on cost-tracker), and a raw 8 KiB byte cut can split a jsonl line, after which P2 fail-opens and delivers nothing. Plan 2.6 also says the relay is inert with an empty queue, which must mean zero stdout bytes, not an empty additionalContext envelope.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan §2.6 Compatibility, §3 New queue FILE FORMAT, §4 P2 drain/cap/fail-open sentences; hooks/hooks.json Stop blocks for opt-in-multiplexer.js and cost-tracker.js; scripts/lib/live-state-dir.js sanitizeSessionId empty-input contract
findings.repair: Specify ts as a JSON number of Unix milliseconds; if payload session_id is missing or empty, skip enqueue and skip drain with no stdout; writers only O_APPEND one complete line; advisory-relay applies the 20-entry and 8 KiB caps after the atomic rename-read by dropping whole oldest lines, drops a single oversize line unread with a debug-log line, and on empty, corrupt, or missing-session drain exits 0 with no stdout.

findings.affected_surface: hooks/opt-in-multiplexer.js merging logic for child permissionDecision values
findings.claim: The multiplexer spec preserves deny/ask but does not explicitly state behavior when a child emits permissionDecision:"allow"; under R3/R10 allow on advisory paths is forbidden, so the implementer needs explicit guidance to avoid an auto-approval regression.
findings.evidence: Plan §3 says "It preserves any deny/ask decision (deny wins over ask) and writes exactly one JSON object" without specifying what happens to allow from a child; the acceptance test only runs two advising children, which exercise additionalContext merging but not an allow case.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/_archive/2026/09/2026-09-26-hook-advisories-reach-model.md §3 multiplexer hard requirement; P1 acceptance; FROZEN_RUBRIC R3, R8, R10
findings.repair: Add one sentence to the multiplexer spec stating that any child-emitted permissionDecision:"allow" is dropped and never propagated (consistent with R3/R10), and extend the multiplexer test with a third case where one advising child emits permissionDecision:"allow" and the merged output asserts no permissionDecision key.

findings.affected_surface: hooks/hooks.json wiring and hooks/README.md row for hooks/advisory-relay.js
findings.claim: R9 and §6 both label advisory-relay as a "new default-on surface", but §3's "New" block says only "hooks/hooks.json wiring" without explicitly stating default-on vs opt-in, leaving the wiring decision ambiguous for the implementer.
findings.evidence: §3 "New" block: "hooks/hooks.json wiring, the hooks/README.md row, and the hook-classes entry if the repo keeps one" — no scope qualifier. R9 risk and §6 both describe the relay as a "new default-on surface". §2.6 calls it "additive" and "inert when nothing is queued" which is consistent with default-on but does not state it.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/_archive/2026/09/2026-09-26-hook-advisories-reach-model.md §3 New block; §2.6 compatibility; §6 risks; FROZEN_RUBRIC R9
findings.repair: In §3, change the wiring bullet to explicitly state "hooks/hooks.json: register advisory-relay (UserPromptSubmit) under the default-on group" and mirror this in the hooks/README.md row so the install/wiring step is unambiguous. No current change; follow-up only.
